title: btrfcomm: Display the associated Service UUID for every packet over an RFCOMM channel
description:
Typically, the RFCOMM channel and associated UUID will have been discovered
by the client during some prior SDP search, within some protocol descriptor list.

Displaying the UUID allows one to e.g. select any packet and immediately know what service
is using that channel, without having to tediously track down the channel's SDP discovery.
This is especially useful for channels carrying unknown/undissected protocols.

Filtering for all connections for a given service, is also much easier now since one
doesn't need to keep track of individual channel numbers.

Whenever the UUID cannot be resolved to a known name, the numeric
UUID (whether 16/32/128-bit) should be displayed, instead of merely "Unknown".

-----

**Before** the proposed change, here's how a channel establishment frame (SABM) appears, alongside the packet details that don't indicate which service is using this channel:

![image](/uploads/a0d09aab86cee10dd1e6b7c97398fe76/image.png){width=900 height=382}

**After** the proposed change, the Service UUID is now displayed both in the SABM info-column, and in the Packet Details (RFCOMM layer) for each packet sent over that channel:

![image](/uploads/d44deeb69b67d8fe5c32483f2ca33ae0/image.png){width=900 height=352}

Filtering by UUID example:

![image](/uploads/34c2d1df32772adc0b16c070f3a2bebc/image.png){width=900 height=351}

Here's a sample capture: [rfc_uuid_test.pcapng](/uploads/a968dcf1f1c16a3dcc4c5957c560041e/rfc_uuid_test.pcapng)
